title: Define enterprise messaging + LTS release notes requirements (slower-change, operational clarity, deprecation policy)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Context
Enterprise/Dedicated/Private customers are asking for a stable runtime line with clear operational guidance. Prior runtime release notes are perceived as noisy and hard to action (SUP-3988) and several deals now have explicit LTS requirements (HubSpot deal_118203).

This ticket defines:
1) External-facing messaging/positioning for the Runtime LTS channel (what it is, what it isn’t)
2) Concrete LTS release notes requirements (structure, risk levels, upgrade instructions, known issues)
3) Deprecation policy expectations for LTS consumers (how we communicate breaking changes, support window, and end-of-support timelines)

## Goals / outcomes
- Enterprise-ready narrative: “slower-change” promise that is specific, measurable, and does not over-commit beyond engineering policy.
- LTS release notes that operations teams can use to make go/no-go decisions quickly.
- A deprecation/compatibility policy section that Sales/CS can confidently reference in contracts and customer comms.

## Non-goals
- Defining the full branching/backport policy (owned by Runtime/Release Eng; see ADR/backport policy work).
- Writing the final docs in Confluence end-to-end (this ticket defines requirements + review criteria; Doc/Eng will publish).

## Requirements (proposed)
### A) Enterprise messaging (public/internal alignment)
- Define audience: Dedicated + Private + regulated workloads where upgrade frequency is constrained.
- Clearly differentiate Standard vs LTS:
  - Standard: faster cadence, features, perf improvements, may include behavior changes behind flags.
  - LTS: patch-only cadence, narrowly scoped fixes (security/correctness/regressions), stronger compatibility posture.
- State guarantees in plain language:
  - Support window (e.g., N months) and what “supported” means (security patches, critical bug fixes, escalation path).
  - Patch cadence target (e.g., monthly or as-needed for security) + emergency patch policy.
  - Compatibility intent (no API breakage; behavior changes only when required for correctness/security; any behavior change must be called out with migration note).
- Explicit exclusions:
  - No new model onboarding commitments in LTS.
  - No large refactors; perf improvements only if regression-related or low-risk and validated via gates.

### B) Release notes requirements (LTS-specific)
Each LTS patch release notes must include:
- Executive summary (2–5 bullets): what changed + why it matters.
- “Operational impact” section:
  - Risk level: Low / Medium / High with rationale.
  - Upgrade time expectation + restart requirements.
  - Any config changes / new flags / defaults.
- Change categories (only customer-relevant):
  - Security fixes (CVE IDs when public; if embargoed, generic description + customer contact path)
  - Correctness fixes
  - Reliability/stability
  - Performance (must include measured deltas + test context)
- Known issues (new + existing):
  - Clear mitigations / workarounds
  - “Not fixed in this patch” list for high-visibility incidents
- Upgrade and rollback guidance:
  - Supported upgrade paths (N-1 patch support)
  - Rollback steps + how to validate health after rollback
- Traceability links:
  - Link to relevant PR(s) and Linear/Jira items (internal) and a customer-safe summary (external)
  - Reference to CI/perf canary evidence location (internal)

### C) Deprecation policy (LTS consumers)
- Define “end of support” (EOS) and “end of life” (EOL) terms and minimum notice period.
- Define how we handle:
  - Deprecation of config fields / flags
  - Removal of compatibility shims
  - Deprecation of underlying GPU/driver baselines (especially for on-prem)
- Communication expectations:
  - Where notices appear: release notes + direct email for Private/Dedicated accounts on LTS
  - Minimum lead time (proposal: >= 90 days for deprecations that require customer action)

## Deliverables
- Requirements doc (this ticket) reviewed and signed off by Runtime + Release Eng + SRE + Support.
- LTS release notes template requirements ready for implementation in changelog tooling (ENG-4826).
- Customer-facing messaging bullets approved for Sales/CS enablement (to be used in PM-813 rollout plan).

## Stakeholders / reviewers
- Product: Lauren Bishop, Vivek Kulkarni
- Release Eng: Connor O’Brien
- Runtime: Noah Patel
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Support: Dev Patel
- Compliance lens: Naomi Feldman (deprecation/EOS terminology)

## Acceptance criteria
- Release notes template includes the required sections and risk-level taxonomy; Release Eng confirms it can be produced from tooling with minimal manual work.
- Sales/CS can answer: “What changes in LTS vs standard?” and “How do I assess upgrade risk?” without ad-hoc engineering involvement.
- Deprecation policy language aligns with support window from ADR (no contradictions).

comments: 2025-11-19 — Marissa Cole: Creating this due to recurring enterprise feedback that runtime notes are too noisy and don’t tell ops what to do. Goal is a minimal, repeatable template that Release Eng can ship every patch without heroics. Pulling in Support + Compliance for terminology (EOS/EOL).

2025-11-20 — Connor O’Brien: +1. Please keep the template strictly LTS-focused; standard channel can remain more verbose. For LTS, we need a small number of sections that are always present. Also, anything that requires manual curation should be optional, not required, or it won’t happen during incident-driven patches.

2025-11-22 — Dev Patel: From Support POV, the missing piece is “Known issues + mitigations” and a clear statement when a fix is NOT included. Customers get upset when they upgrade expecting a fix and it’s not in the patch. Also recommend including “risk level” with a plain-English definition (what makes something high risk).

2025-11-25 — Naomi Feldman: For deprecation language, avoid promising specific timelines without tying it to the LTS support window. Suggest defining: (a) EOS date when we stop producing patches and (b) EOL date when we no longer provide best-effort support. Use minimum notice periods and state that security emergencies may accelerate timelines.

2025-11-27 — Elliot Price: Drafted messaging bullets + a template outline based on previous enterprise docs. Need confirmation from Runtime/SRE on risk level definitions and whether we can always include perf deltas (or only when relevant).

2025-12-02 — Sean Gallagher: Perf deltas should be required only when a perf-related change is included OR when gates detect any regression risk. Otherwise release notes can reference “No material perf delta expected; validated via LTS perf canary suite.” Risk level should map to operational risk (rollback likelihood + blast radius).

2025-12-04 — Vivek Kulkarni: Please add explicit guidance for Private: version pinning semantics and that rollback must be validated against the same model set / traffic replay when possible. Customers in regulated environments need step-by-step, not just “rollback supported.”

2025-12-05 — Marissa Cole: Marking In Review. Incorporating SRE guidance (perf delta rule) and Private-specific notes. Once final, we’ll hand to Connor/Elliot to embed into the Confluence release notes template + the rollout comms plan in PM-813.
